newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil ease from the highs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil ease from the highs.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures eased from the highs on Monday afternoon, with the crude market keeping one eye on NYMEX crude and the other on IPE gas oil.
At 1522 GMT Dec Brent futures were trading 17 cents higher at $23.15 a barrel, just above the day's lows so far.
IPE Nov gas oil was $3.75 a tonne higher at $223.50 after hitting a high of $226.50 early on. The Nov/Dec backwardation narrowed to $7.75 from $8.75 on Friday.
The main fundamental factor behind recent rallies in both markets has been the weather, and the cold snap in Europe and the U.S. northeast lent further support on Monday.
"The freezing weather on both sides of the Atlantic is pushing it up," said one broker.
Low distillate stocks were also supportive, but brokers noted that EU gas oil stocks are expected by analysts to show a modest build in October following the sharp fall in November.
The Euroilstock report for October is due out on Tuesday.
Gas oil is also bolstered by the impending November 1996 contract expiry on Tuesday.
Traders expected anything up to 800,000 tonnes of gas oil to be delivered against the screen.
What happens to that gas oil will partly dictate the onward direction of product and crude markets, they added.
For crude, chartists were looking for support at $22.80 and then at $22.10-$22.15 based on a series of recent lows.
Support for gas oil was expected to emerge at $223.00.
